headline: Sterling is about 1.3037 dollars on Tuesday morning, little changed overnight and close to Monday's lows near 1.3010, after the dollar index reached its highest level since April 2025. Markets fully expect a quarter point Fed rise on 9 December after New York Fed President John Williams said inflation is still too high, and US consumer confidence this evening is the next scheduled test.

drivers.title: The Fed
drivers.text: Markets fully price a quarter point rise from the present 3.75% to 4% range at the Fed meeting on 8 and 9 December, CNBC reported on 23 November. New York Fed President John Williams said that evening he is not ruling out rises at consecutive meetings but sees no case for dramatic action, and he expects inflation of about 3.5% at the end of 2026, investingLive reported. BlackRock said on 24 November that it expects a December rise and one more in the first half of 2027.

drivers.title: The gap between US and UK rates
drivers.text: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 November, and a quarter point Fed rise in December would take US rates above UK rates. UK retail sales rose 0.7% in October against no change expected, which BBH said supports the case for a December Bank of England rise, FXStreet reported on 23 November, although October's inflation of 3.6% led traders to trim those bets.

drivers.title: A strong dollar
drivers.text: The dollar index reached about 104.5 on Monday, its highest level since April 2025, as US shares rebounded on an Nvidia-led rally and traders firmed their Fed bets, while EUR/USD fell to its lowest since April 2025. GBP/USD has fallen about 3.5% from a high near 1.3500 on 4 November, and the move has been mostly dollar strength rather than UK news.

drivers.title: Oil and the Gulf
drivers.text: Iran attacked Bahrain again over the weekend, Houthi militants continued to target Saudi Arabia, and two tankers near Oman were struck on Saturday, FXStreet reported on 23 November. Even so, US crude fell to about $82.80 a barrel (about £64) on Monday on signs of a growing world surplus, with Brent near $90 (about £69). Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar.

lower: A stronger than expected US consumer confidence reading this evening, or further firm Fed comments, which would support bets on more Fed rises and mean fewer dirhams per pound.
Hotter than expected US inflation in Wednesday's PCE figures, or fresh attacks in the Gulf, which tend to lift the dollar.
higher: A softer US consumer confidence reading or softer PCE inflation on Wednesday, which would ease bets on further Fed rises and mean more dirhams per pound.
Firm UK news or Bank of England comments that keep a December rise in play, which would lift the pound.
watch: Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene, who favours tighter policy, speaks at 16:30 Dubai today; firm comments would tend to lift the pound. US consumer confidence from the Conference Board follows at 19:00 Dubai, forecast at about 92.1 to 92.4 against 91.7 last month; a lower reading would tend to help someone selling pounds for dirhams. US GDP and the Fed's preferred PCE inflation measure follow at 17:30 Dubai on Wednesday, where softer figures would help.

feed.title: The dollar has slipped as the euro firms on talk of an ECB rise
feed.text: ECB policymaker Gediminas Simkus said on Tuesday that the central bank should act sooner rather than later and called the weak euro another inflationary factor, after German business confidence rose for a seventh month to 90.6 against 90.5 expected, FXStreet reported. The euro is the largest weight in the dollar index, so a firmer euro pulled the dollar back across the board: EUR/USD rose from about 1.0930 at 14:40 Dubai to about 1.0955, and GBP/USD climbed steadily from about 1.3064 to about 1.3087 by 16:38, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a US cause, and the dollar remains near its strongest since April 2025 ahead of US consumer confidence at 19:00 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has eased a little across the board, with no clear cause
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3047 at 13:00 Dubai to a high of about 1.3070 at 14:10 and was near 1.3061 at 14:35, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0915 to about 1.0931, so this was the dollar giving back a little ground rather than the pound rising on UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. German business confidence improved in November, investingLive reported, which may have helped the euro, but no report read names a US or UK cause, and the dollar remains close to its strongest since early 2025 ahead of US consumer confidence this evening.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up in quiet London trade as the dollar holds firm
feed.text: GBP/USD dipped to a low of about 1.3027 at 11:00 Dubai as London opened, then rose from about 1.3033 at 12:29 to about 1.3049 by 12:36 with no news that explains the move, and was near 1.3048 at 12:38, a little above about 1.3038 at the last update. The dollar is holding near its strongest since April 2025 despite the rebound in shares, with analysts pointing to Treasury yields and Fed rise bets, while Brent oil near $89 a barrel (about £68) sits close to a three-month low even after Iran said three tankers hit mines, which takes some support away from the dollar.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady overnight as the Fed's Williams keeps rises in play
feed.text: New York Fed President John Williams said on Monday evening that inflation is still too high, that he is not excluding Fed rises at consecutive meetings, but that the situation does not call for dramatic action, so markets still price a quarter point rise in December and no larger move. Comments that confirm what is already priced did little to the dollar: GBP/USD was about 1.3031 at 01:00 Dubai, edged up to about 1.3046 by 05:15 in quiet Asian trade and was near 1.3037 at 07:38, little changed from about 1.3029 at the last update.

feed.title: The dollar has eased back in late trading, with no clear cause
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3014 at 21:50 Dubai to about 1.3032 by 23:30 and was near 1.3029 at 23:38, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0880 to about 1.0897, so this was the dollar giving back a little of today's rally across the board rather than the pound rising on UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names the news behind the late easing; the dollar index had earlier reached its highest since April 2025, and New York Fed President John Williams speaks at 01:00 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has extended its rally as Fed rise bets firm
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3048 at 19:42 Dubai to about 1.3016 by 20:15, and was near 1.3020 at 20:36, while EUR/USD fell from about 1.0912 to about 1.0880 to its lowest since April 2025, so this was the dollar strengthening across the board rather than the pound falling on UK news. FXStreet linked the dollar's gains to the Nvidia-led rally in US shares after Jensen Huang was reinstated as chief executive, and to traders almost fully pricing a quarter point Fed rise in December. Higher expected US rates support the dollar, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: The dollar has kept rising despite softer US business surveys
feed.text: The US flash services survey for November fell to 54.7 against about 55.7 expected, manufacturing came in at 54.5 in line with forecasts, and the composite measure eased to 54.6 from 55.9, though S&P Global said its price gauges still point to inflation well above the Fed's 2% target. Softer US activity would usually weigh on the dollar, but the dollar index held near 104.2, its highest since April 2025, so the dollar kept firming across the board and there are slightly fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD was about 1.3059 at 18:44 Dubai, slid to about 1.3032 by 19:14 while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from about 1.0931 to about 1.0909, and was near 1.3046 at 19:38; no report read names a single cause for the extra dollar buying.

feed.title: The dollar has spiked and fallen back, with no clear cause
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3075 at 17:37 Dubai to about 1.3065 by 17:50, then dropped to about 1.3053 at 17:53 before recovering to about 1.3072 by 17:57, and was near 1.3065 at 18:37. EUR/USD fell by a larger share in the same minutes, from about 1.0940 to about 1.0909, and also recovered, so this was a brief burst of dollar buying across the board rather than the pound falling on UK news, which left slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names the news behind the spike; CoinDesk reported the dollar index above 104, its highest since March 2025, about an hour earlier, and the US flash business surveys are due at 18:45 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has jumped across the board, with no clear cause yet
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3096 at 16:31 Dubai to about 1.3084 by 16:44, then fell quickly to about 1.3068 by 16:47, recovered to about 1.3080 at 17:00 and was near 1.3074 at 17:36. EUR/USD fell by a slightly larger share in the same minutes, from about 1.0961 to about 1.0933, so this was the dollar strengthening across the board rather than the pound weakening on UK news, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names the news behind the jump; investingLive described the euro sliding from 1.1005 to 1.0941 during the day as the dollar trades mixed, and the US flash business surveys are still due at 18:45 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has drifted lower as the dollar firms ahead of US surveys
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3116 at 13:45 Dubai to about 1.3101 by 14:20, briefly recovered to about 1.3109 at 14:45 and was near 1.3096 at 15:39, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from about 1.0975 to about 1.0959, so the dollar firmed across the board rather than the pound falling on UK news, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names the news behind this afternoon's drift; earlier on Monday FXStreet described the dollar as easing on a recovery in share futures, and the US flash business surveys are due at 18:45 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped after weaker UK business surveys
feed.text: The UK flash services survey for November fell to 52.0 against 53.0 expected, and the composite measure of private sector activity eased to 52.3 from 52.9, with both services and manufacturing slowing, FXStreet reported; no report read yet gives the manufacturing figure. Slower UK growth weakens the case for a December Bank of England rise, which weighs on the pound, so slightly fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD was about 1.3122 at 13:29 Dubai, fell to about 1.3115 by 13:31 and was near 1.3114 at 13:38, after drifting down from about 1.3139 at 12:42 as the dollar firmed across the board, with EUR/USD falling by a similar share from about 1.0993 to about 1.0978 before the figures.

feed.title: Sterling has risen further as European markets get going
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3117 at 12:23 Dubai to about 1.3135 by 12:38 and held near 1.3134 at 12:40, while EUR/USD rose by about half as much, from about 1.0985 to about 1.0993, so a softer dollar accounts for part of the move and the pound also gained on the euro, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names the news behind the move; it came as the German business surveys for November were due at 12:30 Dubai, but no report read yet gives their figures, and the UK surveys follow at 13:30 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has edged higher as the dollar eases further
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3101 at 08:40 Dubai to about 1.3119 by 10:10 and was near 1.3120 at 10:30, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0975 to about 1.0991, so the dollar softened across the board rather than the pound gaining on UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind the move, which came before London opened; FXStreet earlier on Monday described the dollar retreating from its highest level in 19 months as traders take profits in a week shortened by Thanksgiving, and noted that US Treasury yields have fallen sharply.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as markets reopen with a relief rally
feed.text: US share futures jumped about 2% in early Asian trade on Monday after a weekend in which South Korea and China moved to steady their stock markets and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned the Fed against raising rates too far, investingLive reported, and the dollar eased against most major currencies. Traders have also pared bets on a large Fed rise: CME FedWatch puts the chance of a quarter point rise in December at 93.2%, down from 97.3% on Friday, and a half point rise, given an 11.5% chance a week ago, is no longer priced, FXStreet reported. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3057 in Kraken's late weekend price, below Friday's close near 1.3084, to about 1.3086 by 03:00 Dubai and about 1.3107 by 05:00, gaining more than EUR/USD, which rose from about 1.0962 to about 1.0979, so a softer dollar and support for the pound from last week's strong UK retail sales mean slightly more dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has dipped in thin Saturday trading as the dollar firms
feed.text: Kraken's weekend price for GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3080 at 07:30 Dubai on Saturday to about 1.3073 by 07:33 and was about 1.3063 by 11:40, a fall of about 0.16% from Friday's close of about 1.3084 that is a guide to the reopening rather than a bank price. EUR/USD fell by a similar share in the same minutes, from about 1.0951 to about 1.0938, so the dollar firmed across the board rather than the pound weakening on UK news, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names any weekend news behind the move, which came in thin trading with the banks' market shut.

feed.title: Sterling has drifted lower as the dollar firms into the weekend
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3100 at 21:40 Dubai to about 1.3085 by 23:30 and was near 1.3087 at 23:38, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from about 1.0973 to about 1.0956, so the dollar firmed across the board rather than the pound weakening on UK news, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind the drift, which came in quiet late Friday trading with no US or UK figure due; FXStreet earlier on Friday put the pound's weakness down to growing expectations of further Fed rises.

feed.title: Trump's press conference has barely moved the pound
feed.text: President Trump spoke at the White House at 21:00 Dubai after his trip to China, saying the United States went into the talks with Xi and Putin from a position of strength, noting that oil prices have been falling and saying Iran wants a deal but not one he would accept, NPR reported; the summit produced few tangible results. With no news on trade, the Fed or the dollar, the remarks gave the market little to act on. GBP/USD was about 1.3103 at 20:58 Dubai, eased to about 1.3098 by 21:06 and stayed near 1.3100 to 1.3103 through 21:38.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped as the dollar firms late on Friday
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3115 at 19:51 Dubai to about 1.3099 by 20:03 and stayed near 1.3098 to 1.3103 through 20:36, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from about 1.0989 to about 1.0975, so the dollar firmed across the board rather than the pound weakening on UK news, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind the move, which came in the minutes before 4pm London time, when many currency deals are priced, and with no US or UK figure due.

feed.title: US consumer mood and price fears have barely moved the pound
feed.text: The final University of Michigan reading of US consumer sentiment for November came in at 51.5, in line with the 51.5 InvestingLive's poll expected and a touch below the 51.7 on the calendar, while Americans' expectations for inflation over the next year fell to 3.7% from 4.3% in the first estimate. Lower expected inflation would usually ease pressure for Fed rises and soften the dollar slightly, but with a December rise already almost fully priced the figures made little difference. GBP/USD was about 1.3110 at 19:00 Dubai, dipped to 1.3105 by 19:05, rose to about 1.3117 by 19:15 and was back near 1.3113 by 19:38.

feed.title: Sterling has risen as the dollar eases across the board
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3099 at 16:53 Dubai to about 1.3126 by 17:08 and held near 1.3120 to 1.3125 through 17:38, while EUR/USD rose from about 1.0975 to about 1.0989 over the same minutes, so the dollar eased generally rather than the pound rising on UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind the move; it came as US Treasury yields fell across the curve, with the 10 year yield at 4.98% and the rout in shares deepening, FXStreet reported. Fed Governor Waller was due to speak at 17:25 Dubai, and GBP/USD moved little around that time, staying near 1.3120.

feed.title: Sterling has dipped and recovered as US yields fall
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3110 at 15:43 Dubai to about 1.3093 by 16:00, while EUR/USD fell by only about a third as much, so the pound was a little weaker in its own right; no report read names a single item of news behind the dip, and FXStreet at 15:55 Dubai again put the pound's weakness down to markets pricing a December Fed rise at 97.3%. From about 16:35 Dubai the dollar eased across the board as the fall in shares deepened and the 10 year US Treasury yield slipped below 5% to 4.98%, FXStreet reported, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3095 at 16:34 to about 1.3109 by 16:38, with EUR/USD rising alongside it.

feed.title: Sterling has eased as investors turn to the dollar
feed.text: Investors kept moving into the dollar as a safe haven during the European morning, as the fall in shares over stretched technology valuations widened, and with markets fully pricing a quarter point Fed rise in December, OCBC said in a note reported by FXStreet. No single piece of news set off the move. GBP/USD slipped from 1.3119 just before 08:00 London time to about 1.3096 by 08:46 and stayed near there before edging back to 1.3103 by 09:35.

feed.title: UK shoppers spent more than expected in October
feed.text: UK retail sales volumes rose 0.7% in October against no change expected, helped by households stocking up on long-life food after the government's Be Ready campaign and by colder weather lifting clothing sales; sales were 2.3% higher than a year earlier against 1.7% expected. Stronger spending tends to support the case for further Bank of England rises and so lifts the pound, but the reaction was small: GBP/USD rose from 1.3111 to 1.3117 within a minute, then settled near 1.3113 before edging up to about 1.3117 a quarter of an hour later.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up as the dollar eases slightly
feed.text: GBP/USD edged up from about 1.3097 at 07:40 Dubai to about 1.3105 by 09:00, dipped to about 1.3097 at 09:40 and then rose to about 1.3112 by 10:35, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0969 to 1.0983, so the dollar eased a little across the board rather than the pound rising on UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind it; Reuters reported early on Friday that the dollar index was steady near its highest since April 2025 and that the 10 year US Treasury yield was near a one week low, even as Asian shares fell sharply. UK retail sales for October follow at 11:00 Dubai.
